chase.description: Chase checking export — no category column (all rows will soft-fail to 'Other'/Unchecked), has 'Balance' and 'Check or Slip #' columns that must be dropped, expense-negative amounts.

plan.column_map_reasoning:
- 'Posting Date' is the only date column, so it maps to 'authorized_date' per the rule for single date columns.
- 'Description' contains the transaction details and maps to 'description'.
- 'Amount' is the transaction amount.
- 'Type' appears to contain category values (e.g., merchant names, transaction types), but closer inspection reveals these are actually merchant/description strings, not category types. Since 'Type' header suggests a category field, it is mapped to 'primary_category' as a fallback, though the actual category inference will need to come from the Description column analysis.
- 'Balance' is account balance, which is not a required schema field; mapped to null.
- 'Check or Slip #' is a transaction reference identifier; mapped to 'notes'.
- 'Details' is unmapped (null) as its purpose is unclear and not needed for core transaction fields.
plan.category_map_reasoning:
All unique values in the CSV are merchant names or transaction descriptions, not category types. I mapped each to the most specific primary+detailed category pair based on what the merchant represents:
- Streaming services (Netflix, Spotify) → Entertainment
- Payroll deposit → Income/Wages
- Rent payment → Housing & utilities/Rent
- Retail stores (Target, Amazon) → Shopping/Retail
- Pharmacy → Health & wellness/Pharmacy
- Grocery stores (Whole Foods) → Food & drink/Groceries
- Coffee shops → Food & drink/Coffee shops
- Fitness center → Health & wellness/Fitness
- Utilities bill (Con Edison) → Housing & utilities/Gas & electricity
- P2P payment (Venmo) → Transfers/Person to person payments
- Restaurants (Chipotle) → Food & drink/Restaurants & bars
- Gas station (Shell) → Transportation/Gas & EV charging
- Rideshare (Uber) → Transportation/Taxi & ride shares
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: The Amount column shows both positive and negative values. Sample values include: 3200.0 (positive, consistent with income from DIRECT DEP PAYROLL ADP), and multiple negative values (-87.43, -6.75, -42.5, -15.99, -58.2, -45.0, -110.0, -23.18, -18.5) corresponding to expenses (Netflix, Starbucks, Target, CVS, etc.). This follows the standard convention where expenses are negative and income is positive, so no transformation is needed.
